title: A whole walk run gets past the 1080p export walk
goal: Every full walk run since the export speed-up stops dead right after the walk that exports a five minute recording at 1080p: the next walks cannot start the app, the run gives up as blind, and about 460 of 653 walks never run. A blind run does not count as a sweep, so the loop starts the whole thing again after the next task and loses another fifty minutes the same way.
notes:
Reproduced by the daily digest 2026-09-28. Both full runs that day (queue/sweep/2026-09-28-030406.log and 2026-09-28-042334.log) went blind at the same place: export-a-video-at-1080p-walk ok in about 100s, then export-card-while-writing-walk, export-keeps-to-the-in-and-out-walk, export-quality-walk, export-webp-walk, extract-a-marked-stretch-walk all 'COULD NOT START the probe would not launch'. Ran by hand, nothing else using the probe:

$ Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build export-a-video-at-1080p-walk export-card-while-writing-walk export-keeps-to-the-in
export-a-video-at-1080p-walk               99s  ok
export-card-while-writing-walk              0s  COULD NOT START  the probe would not launch, so nothing ran this walk
export-keeps-to-the-in-and-out-walk         0s  COULD NOT START  the probe would not launch, so nothing ran this walk
==> 1 passed, 0 failed, 2 could not start

Then on its own: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/export-card-while-writing-walk.json --no-build -> status ok in 78s. So the walks are fine and it is what the 1080p walk leaves behind. playtest-all.sh swallows probe-app.sh's own message (out=$(...) and only the verdict is printed), so the first step is to see it: likely candidates are the '!! Probe did not come up' branch (5s of pgrep after open -g) while the last probe is still quitting or still writing its export. No crash report was written at either time (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports). Likely started with 44fde13f (five minute export in a quarter of its length) or 799ef6a2 (busy MP4 size), both 2026-09-28, which changed how export writes.
acceptance: Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build export-a-video-at-1080p-walk export-card-while-writing-walk export-keeps-to-the-in runs all three walks and none reads COULD NOT START
The reason the app would not start after the export walk is named in this task's log, from what probe-app.sh printed, not guessed

A walk that leaves the app busy (an export still writing, a slow quit) cannot stop the next walk from launching: either the walk waits for its own work to finish or the launcher waits for the last app to be gone

A whole-set run that went blind is not started again on the same commit: queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs decide() has no memory of a blind run today, so after one the loop starts another full run before the next task (2026-09-28 lost two 50 minute runs this way), and its drill covers the new rule
The next full walk run covers the whole set without going blind

log.note: digest 2026-09-28: sweep.sh status says a full sweep is still owed (26.8h since the last whole-set run), so the loop will most likely start a third run before claiming this task and go blind at the same walk again. Acceptance widened: a blind run must not be started again on the same commit.

Reason, from what probe-app.sh printed (Scripts/playtest.sh on export-card-while-writing-walk straight after the 1080p walk): '_LSOpenURLsWithCompletionHandler() failed for the application .../Photonz Probe.app with error -600.' The last probe was still EXITING: ps showed it as '82692 ?E (Photonz Probe)'. An exiting process drops its command line, so quit_probe's 'pgrep -f Photonz Probe.app/Contents/MacOS' stopped matching at 0.06s while lsappinfo still listed the bundle (timed: pgrep false at 0.06s, lsappinfo true until 0.61s on one run; the first run lingered for several seconds). open then asks LaunchServices, which still has the app, and answers -600 (procNotFound). Only the export walks tear down enough (Metal, VideoToolbox: 74 of 75 samples had an iokit_user_client_trap thread) for the window to be hit. No crash, the app is fine.

Fix: Scripts/probe-app.sh quit_probe now remembers the pids, waits with kill -0 (sees an exiting process) AND for lsappinfo to drop com.dzearing.photonz.probe, SIGKILL after 15s; the open is retried twice after another quit_probe if it still fails. Verified: Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build export-a-video-at-1080p-walk export-card-while-writing-walk export-keeps-to-the-in -> 98s ok, 82s ok, 21s ok, 3 passed.

Blind rerun rule: queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs decide() takes blind.json; a blind run newer than latest.json on the same code (same head, or only queue/ changed since, which the digest commit did today) gets one rotating check and then nothing until code lands; request --now still wins. 8 new checks in queue/bin/sweep-schedule-drill.mjs, all pass. Before the commit, sweep.sh why-not read 'slice: the whole set went blind on this commit...' where it had read 'full: 27.0h'. playtest-all.sh now prints the launcher's reason under a COULD NOT START line; sweep-parse reads such a log identically (checked).

Last acceptance item (next full run covers the whole set without going blind) cannot be run inside a task: requested a sweep; sweep.sh why-not now says 'full: 27.1h since the last whole-set run', so the loop's next full run is the check. If it goes blind again, sweep.sh status and the COULD NOT START line will now name the launcher's reason.

Probe launcher (Scripts/probe-app.sh) now waits for the last probe to be gone from the process table and from LaunchServices before opening the next one; the cause was open's error -600 while the probe was still exiting after the 1080p export walk. The three export walks now run back to back: 98s ok, 82s ok, 21s ok. A blind whole-set run is no longer rerun on the same code (sweep-schedule decide + drill), and COULD NOT START lines carry the launcher's reason. Scripts/test.sh 10265 passed. Commit 7046403c. The whole-set check is requested and due next; not yet observed.
